title: Tale of the Richard Who Married His Beautiful Daughter to the Poor Old Man

keywords: tale of the richard who married his beautiful daughter to the poor old man
full_text:
An affluent merchant of Baghdad had an only daughter named Salma, whose beauty was matched by her profound learning in literature, mathematics, and ethics. Wealthy young emirs and boastful merchants courted her with gifts of pearls and golden carriages, but Salma rejected them all, seeking a husband whose character was steadfast and pure.

Her father, sharing her wisdom, visited the Great Academy of Baghdad and observed an elderly, modest scholar named Abu Bakr, who taught the poor without fee and lived in quiet contentment.

The merchant invited the scholar to his mansion and offered him his daughter’s hand in marriage with a handsome dowry!

The neighbors were astonished, mocking the merchant: 'Why do you bestow your radiant young daughter upon a poor, gray-bearded scholar, when wealthy young emirs knock upon your gate?'

The merchant replied with calm authority: 'I looked upon the young emirs, and I saw men whose wealth was inherited, whose minds were empty, and whose pride would bring domestic tyranny into my home.

I looked upon this scholar, and I saw a man of unshakeable integrity, gentle speech, and profound wisdom. If my daughter weeps, he will comfort her with philosophy; if misfortune strikes, his faith will sustain her; and in his house, she will be an honored queen, not a gilded toy.'

Salma and the scholar lived in radiant intellectual and domestic harmony for thirty years, proving that a marriage founded on character and wisdom outlasts all the fleeting illusions of youth and gold.
moral: Choose character, wisdom, and moral integrity over mere youth and fleeting gold.
